With helpers, deputies, toy-shops, reindeer, and his sledge, he continues making and distributing gifts so that children, poor or rich, may receive happiness.

l: the Law, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: prohibits a mortal being adopted by an immortal [from then onward] The Law forbids an immortal from adopting a mortal. Ak relaxes the Law to allow Necile to keep the infant, but declares that it will never again be relaxed for this purpose.

l: the World, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: The World contains broad forests, grows older as its population increases and spreads, clears forests for cities, fields, and cattle, and reaches its end.

l: Fairy Queen, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: The Fairy Queen, queen of the fairies, promises on Christmas Eve to protect the deer while away from the Forest, then sends Fairies to recover toys stolen and hidden by the Awgwas.

l: immortals, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: The immortals are supernatural rulers of the earth and servants of the world, subject to Ak. After Claus leaves Burzee, they direct him toward the Laughing Valley, where friendly beings support him; they favor his plan and befriend him for serving children. Though they fear and avoid the Awgwas, their friendship protects Claus through Fairy rescue and guarding Seals. In old age, they gather in Burzee, unanimously grant Santa Claus immortality, and bestow the Mantle upon him.

l: Claus's adoption by Necile, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Necile's adoption of Claus is permitted and sanctioned by Ak, while the forest nymphs' adoption with her draws interest from Ryls, Knooks, and Fairies unfamiliar with immortals adopting a human child.

l: journey through the world, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus, companion and pupil of Ak, is taken on a world journey from the Forest of Burzee to cities and dwellings of men. Though Necile grieves and Claus is honored, he observes humanity across regions and occupations, farmers, warriors, merchants, and children, then returns to Burzee transformed from an ever-joyous boy into a grave, thoughtful youth.

l: Master Woodsman, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: The Master Woodsman of the World holds authority over the Forest’s protection, his word being law. He grants and preserves Claus’s protection and powers, guides him mercifully toward and after his new home among men, promises other beings’ service, and provides support through Nelko, an ax, Fairies, supplies, and clothing.

l: Laughing Valley, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: The Laughing Valley of Hohaho is a happy, peaceful valley at the eastern edge of Burzee, between rolling green hills, with a brook wandering through it. Filled with grass, wildflowers, bees, butterflies, happiness, peace, and good-will, it has long awaited Claus as its tenant. Its cheerful natural life restores his merriment, and he chooses it as his home, dwelling, workshop, and the place where he makes and stores toys. Winter brings heavy snow that covers his cottage and hinders his visits to children, but after storms pass he travels from the Valley to help others. In warmer times its brook, grass, sun, and other features seem to laugh, inspiring Claus to sing, laugh, and whistle. Visitors, including Bessie’s cavalcade, come to his dwelling, while the Awgwas block children from reaching it. The Valley becomes a battlefield when Ak gathers the immortals there; they defeat the Awgwas and their allies. Claus also begins and ends his first reindeer journey there, and leaves and returns there on Christmas Eve after distributing toys. After many healthy years, when Santa Claus becomes old and weak, the once-merry Valley is hushed and mournful.

l: Claus's departure from the Forest, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus's departure ends his sweet, wild life in the Forest. Turning away instead of formally saying goodbye, he leaves the Forest people, passes through Burzee, and goes to the world of men for his mission.

l: Santa Claus's mission to bring happiness to children, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Santa Claus's mission to bring happiness to children begins when Claus leaves the forest, resolves to care for mankind's children, and hopes their joy will preserve Necile's kindness in memory. On his first Christmas Eve, he delivers toys to sleeping children. For hundreds of years, he makes and distributes toys worldwide with the immortals' assistance and goodwill, until old age prevents him from making more toys.

l: brook, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: A pure, playful laughing brook in the Laughing Valley of Hohaho, free after winter, gives Claus drinking water as its ripples race and sing.

l: Forest, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: The Forest in Burzee contains nymphs who guard it and is home to deer guarded by the Knooks. It teaches Claus that living trees are sacred and feeling, leading him to use fallen trees. Claus knows Flossie and Glossie there; after journeys, the deer return by daybreak and may bathe in its Pool of Nares.

l: house (Claus's house), The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus's house is a strong, roomy dwelling built overnight by the Knooks from his logs, with a furnished large room around a fireplace and a smaller room containing his bed and dried moss.

l: Spirit of Happiness, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: enters Claus's heart [while he sleeps] The Spirit of Happiness enters Claus's heart while he sleeps in the Valley. It drives out his terror, care, and misgivings so that he will no longer be clouded by anxiety.

l: field flowers, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Field flowers, tended and protected by the Ryls, grow throughout the Valley; timid at first, they remain valued by Claus for their songs and beauty.

l: food supplies, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: are_provided_by Ryls of the Field Flowers [for Claus] The Ryls of the Field Flowers provide Claus with food supplies so he will not have to cultivate the ground. These supplies include fresh milk, bread, honey, apples, and grapes, and they remain available whenever he is hungry.

l: Happiness, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Happiness fills the Laughing Valley and is expressed by the brook, daffodils, sunbeams, and other living things. Claus recognizes the Valley as a place of happiness, joy, peace, and good-will.

l: Claus's life in the Laughing Valley, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: is_supported_by the immortals [with favor and friendship] Claus's life in the Laughing Valley begins with the favor and friendship of the immortals. His house, food, clothing, firewood, and other needs are supplied, allowing him to live peacefully while preparing to do good work.

l: Jack Frost, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Jack Frost is a jolly sprite, son and agent of the Frost King, who knows Claus from the Forest and nips noses, ears, and toes in winter. Visiting Claus at night, he boasts of nipping many people but promises to spare children if he can resist temptation.

l: Blinkie, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Blinkie is a large, real cat with soft glossy fur who belongs to Claus after Peter the Knook gives her to him. She purrs continually and serves as Claus’s model while he carves and paints a wooden cat. Initially angry and later offended by the toy’s attention, she recognizes it is wood, resumes admiring Claus, hides from wind, and is terrified by Shiegra’s snarl.

l: toy cat, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: The first toy is a wooden cat carved by Claus from a stick of firewood on a long winter evening, modeled after Blinkie with a head, body, haunches, tail, ears, eyes, and nose. It is painted black, with red lips and tongue, green eyes, yellow, and blue on its wooden ribbon. Claus is pleased, Blinkie reacts to it, Weekum likes its harmlessness, and a colored toy cat comforts a sick girl.

l: winter, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Winter arrives in Laughing Valley after flowers fade and insects depart, covers it with snow, keeps Claus indoors, where boredom leads him to carve wood, then is over.

l: villages, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: In a village Claus has never visited, he discovers that the locked doors prevent ordinary entry. With the deer's help, he reaches the rooftops, visits the houses through their chimneys, and leaves toys for every sleeping child.

l: snow, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Snow covers Claus's dwelling and Laughing Valley in winter, lies many feet deep, and is frozen hard by the Frost King so deer and sledge can travel; it supports their rapid journey home before Claus tumbles into a snowdrift.

l: Weekum, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Weekum is a little boy living beyond Laughing Valley who becomes lost walking to his auntie’s house in a snowstorm. Claus finds and cares for him, gives him a wooden toy cat, and Weekum takes it home to his mother.

l: colored toy-making, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus’s toy-making begins with colored wooden cats made to delight children without scratching or biting. As his skill grows, it expands into rabbits, lambs, other animal figures, dolls, drums, cymbals, whistles, and horns. The Knooks supply wood, the Ryls supply paints and brushes, and the Fairies bring tools, enabling continuous work in his workshop through winter.

l: sick girl, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: A little girl lies ill with fever and pain on a wretched cot in a poor hut near the Lord of Lerd’s palace; Claus gives her a colored wooden cat that comforts, heals, and lets her sleep.

l: wooden lioness, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: A wooden lioness, carved and painted by Claus in Shiegra's likeness, has fierce teeth, frowning lines, a crouching body, and a long tail; Shiegra approves it for children.

l: rescue of Weekum, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: is_a rescue [performed by Claus during a snowstorm] During a snowstorm, Claus hears a cry of distress and finds Weekum buried in a snowdrift. He carries the child into his house, warms and feeds him, lets him sleep with the wooden cat, and returns him safely to his mother the next morning.

l: Mayrie, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Mayrie is a poor small girl and child with a younger brother who loves a wooden rabbit and wants toy cats. She visits Claus, cries when her brother receives the only ready cat, and is frightened by Shiegra's image. Claus later makes her a cat; after she breaks it, he gives her Bessie, which delights her.

l: Mayrie's younger brother, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Mayrie's younger brother, a small child, receives Claus's last toy cat after echoing Mayrie's request, then drops it while fleeing Shiegra's image in fear.

l: Shiegra's image, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Shiegra's image is a toy depicting Shiegra, with fierce teeth and glaring eyes. Claus offers it to Mayrie, frightens both children, then locks it away and rejects fierce toy models.

l: toy cats, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus creates toy cats popular with children, giving them to Mayrie's brother and town children, then carving and painting one for Mayrie.

l: toys, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Toys are playthings made by Claus for children of the world, intended to be loved rather than feared. He first gives toy animals to visiting children; after Mayrie becomes frightened, he favors gentler squirrels, rabbits, deer, lambkins, wooden rabbits, and wooden lambs. As children multiply and spread, Claus makes toys in larger quantities, aided by Kilter, Peter, Nuter, and Wisk. The toys bring happiness and encourage obedience, protecting children from the Awgwas' influence, though the Awgwas steal them until they are destroyed. Claus then carries toys safely to dwellings and villages. Over time his work becomes increasingly beautiful: dolls may say "papa" and "mama," lambs squeak, birds whistle, horses have wheels, and a donkey nods. He yearly loads toys for children, and when chimneys prevent delivery, the little folk, parents, and toy-shops help distribute them.

l: children, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Children are little and helpless, living in villages, including those Claus visits. They travel to Claus’s house for his wonderful toys, creating a path from the plain to his cottage, while he also brings gifts to sick or crippled children. The Awgwas influence them to quarrel, disobey, and behave badly, though Claus’s toys make them happier and more obedient; after he stops visiting villages, the Awgwas keep them from finding the Laughing Valley. Claus later brings toys to children everywhere, including those who have never owned one, delivering playthings to sleeping children in villages and a city. Children find the toys by their beds, learn that Santa Claus brought them, and are taught to pray for forgiveness when naughty. They receive his toys with love and begin hanging stockings by fireplaces on Christmas Eve after Margot, Dick, Ned, and Sara find toys in theirs.

l: immortals, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Immortals are beings who live forever in the Forest of Burzee, supporting and protecting Claus. When evil Awgwas threaten him, they unite in the Laughing Valley, defeat evil, and return to their forest duties.

l: Mayrie's fright, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: is_caused_by Shiegra's image Mayrie's fright begins when she sees the fierce teeth and glaring eyes of Shiegra's image. Her terror causes her and her brother to flee, and it teaches Claus that children's toys should be mild and pleasant rather than fierce.

l: Bessie Blithesome, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Bessie Blithesome, a rich lord’s young daughter, visits Claus escorted by men-at-arms, saying she has no toy. He gives her a clay nymph doll, her first toy; she loves it as her baby and adopts the stockings custom.

l: toy nymph, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: A clay toy nymph resembling Necile is formed, sun-baked, painted, and given by Claus to Bessie, who loves and calls it a dolly.

l: Bessie image dolly, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: A clay toy resembling Bessie Blithesome is made by Claus, baked hard, dressed in lavender silk and lace, painted with her features, and given to Mayrie.

l: toy, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Bessie asks Claus for a toy because there are no toys in the world but his. Claus first promises her the next toy he makes, and the toy nymph becomes the gift that delights her.

l: riches, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: is_a gown [that may be put on or taken away] Claus initially thinks riches provide enough comforts that rich children should not need his toys. Necile explains that riches are like a removable gown and do not change the child beneath them.

l: children's happiness, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Children's happiness is available to rich and poor alike and is sought by Santa Claus for every child if possible. It matters more than thoughtless parents' wishes or indifference, and Santa Claus works with helpers, parents, and toy-shops to preserve it through gifts.

l: Claus's decision to make toys for all children, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus decides that rich and poor children alike may claim his services, and he begins making toys for Bessie and poor children to support children's happiness.

l: creation of the first dolly, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus unintentionally shapes moist clay into a head resembling Necile, then develops it into a toy nymph with hair, an oak-leaf gown, sandals, painted eyes, teeth, lips, and hair. The baked and painted figure becomes the first dolly, which he gives to Bessie.

l: Mayrie receiving the dolly, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Mayrie receives the silk-robed Bessie image dolly from Claus after her toy cat breaks, loves it, and happily carries it home.

l: Awgwas, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Awgwas are a gigantic, transient race of evil creatures, neither mortal nor immortal. Invisible to ordinary people but visible to immortals, they live in rocky mountains, travel swiftly through the air, hate mankind, and devote themselves to wickedness. Without conscience, they influence mortals and naughty children toward anger, quarrels, and bad acts; mortals cannot harm them, while immortals avoid them in fear. They choose King Awgwa by the most horrible proposed deed and obey him. They attack and persecute Claus, steal his toys, and hide them in a rock-covered mountain cave, though Fairies later open it. Refusing to stop and defying Ak, they summon allies for war; immortals destroy them, leaving earthen hillocks, and they perish from earth.

l: King Awgwa, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: King Awgwa, leader and king of the Awgwas, is a wicked creature who plots to remove Claus from the children because Claus's toys make them less vulnerable. He orders failed attempts to abduct, imprison, rob, or destroy Claus, then leads an army against the immortals. After threatening Claus, he is cleaved in two by Ak's gleaming ax.

l: the Awgwas' wickedness, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: The Awgwas' wickedness includes inspiring angry passions, encouraging children to eat unripe fruit and disobey their parents, and taking pleasure in their suffering and punishment. They also attack Claus because his work limits their power over children.

l: the Awgwas' plot against Claus, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: aims_to_destroy Claus [by removing him from children] The Awgwas' plot is to remove Claus from the children by abducting him, imprisoning him, stealing his toys, and blocking children from reaching him. Their attempts fail to destroy Claus, but they succeed for a time in keeping him from delivering his toys.

l: Claus's abduction, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus's abduction is a repeated forcible seizure by the Awgwas: they bind sleeping Claus and abandon him in an Ethop jungle, then capture him again and imprison him in a mountain cave.

l: Claus's escape, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Claus's escape is his rescue from the jungle by the Knooks and return from an Awgwa mountain-cave prison by Fairies, both transporting him home to the Laughing Valley.

l: war between the immortals and the spirits of evil, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: War between good immortals and evil spirits begins when the Awgwas defy Ak and threaten Claus, ending with the immortals defeating them and their allies in the Laughing Valley.

l: spirits of evil, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: is_a evil spirits [opposed by the immortals] The spirits of evil are summoned by the King Awgwa to fight the immortals and include Asiatic Dragons, Tatary Giants, Black Demons, Goozzle-Goblins, and mountain Awgwas. Their forces are defeated, with only some of the Giants escaping.

l: Prince of the Knooks, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: Prince of the Knooks is the ruler and king of the Knooks in Burzee. On Christmas Eve, he permits Claus to use up to ten deer for one night each year, requires their return by daybreak, names them reindeer, and secures their protection through the Fairy Queen.

l: Law, The Life and Adventures of Santa Claus
s: states Good cannot be overthrown by Evil [when opposed to Evil] The Law states that Evil may accomplish terrible deeds when unopposed, but the powers of Good cannot be overthrown when opposed to Evil. The text says that the King Awgwa's ignorance of this Law costs him his existence.
